summary: Show a polycrystal as differently oriented lattice domains and make slip planes a property of orientation rather than a texture.
objective: Build a polycrystalline block where each grain has its own lattice orientation and I can reveal the slip planes that follow it.
intent_signals: Show why a metal has grains with different orientations.
Explain slip planes and grain boundaries in a 3D block.
example_prompts: Build a polycrystalline block with per-grain lattice orientation and toggleable slip planes.
Show a dislocation stepping through a lattice plane and where a grain boundary interrupts it.
negative_signals: Not a crystal plasticity or finite-element solver: no stress, strain or yield strength is computed.
Not a materials-selection or failure-analysis tool.
not_for: Not a crystal plasticity or finite-element solver: no stress, strain or yield strength is computed.
Not a materials-selection or failure-analysis tool.

entities.name: Grain domains
entities.guidance: Partition the block into grains as closed cells with shared boundary faces, each storing its own lattice orientation.

entities.name: Lattice and slip planes
entities.guidance: Draw a sparse lattice inside a selected grain and derive the highlighted plane from that grain orientation, so the plane rotates with the grain.

entities.name: Dislocation marker
entities.guidance: Show one dislocation line and its step-by-step advance along a plane, stopping visibly at the grain boundary.

state_contract.model: Grain list with orientations, a boundary set shared between neighbouring grains, and a dislocation position expressed as a step index on a chosen plane. Deformation shown is an authored illustration, not a computed response to load.
state_contract.authority: Grain orientation is authoritative: lattice, slip plane and dislocation direction are all derived from it, so changing an orientation must update all three together.
actions: Select a grain and show its lattice and available slip planes.
Step a dislocation along the selected plane.
Toggle the grain boundary surfaces and the outer block faces.
Reset orientations and the dislocation to the authored start.

invariants: A slip plane never crosses a grain boundary unchanged; at the boundary the plane orientation changes or the marker stops.
Neighbouring grains share one boundary surface rather than each owning a private copy.
Stepping the dislocation backwards restores the previous lattice state exactly.
motion_guidance: Advance the dislocation in discrete lattice steps so the motion reads as bond-by-bond, not as a sliding decal.
Do not deform the whole block continuously as if a load were applied; any shape change is an authored illustration.
known_limits: Illustrative microstructure: grain sizes, shapes and orientation distribution are authored, not from a measured sample.
The recipe shows one dislocation on one plane; multiplication, tangles and cross-slip are out of scope.
Authored guidance only: no scene runtime, rendering or numerical calibration has been run for this recipe.

claims.statement: Grain boundaries are internal interfaces between zones of a crystalline material that have different lattice alignments.
claims.scope: Definition of the interface as stated in the cited session material; grain size effects are not claimed.

source_refs.locator: Session 20 summary, two-dimensional defects and grain boundaries

claims.statement: Movement of dislocations through the lattice contributes to plastic deformation and work hardening.
claims.scope: Qualitative mechanism quoted from the cited session objectives. The same page summarises the yield-stress argument in an elliptical sentence, so no quantitative strength or yield claim is drawn from this source.

source_refs.locator: Session 20 learning objectives and summary, dislocation motion and yield stress

object_craft.structure: Convex-ish cells with flat shared faces and slightly bevelled edges so boundaries read as surfaces rather than as wireframes.
object_craft.material: One metal family with per-grain variation in orientation-driven shading rather than arbitrary colour, so the block still looks like a single material.
object_craft.articulation: None. Grains are static; only visibility and selection change.

object_craft.structure: Sparse atom markers on the lattice with a translucent plane patch bounded by the grain, not extending past it.
object_craft.material: Thin translucent plane with a visible border so it can be seen edge-on; lattice markers stay small enough to avoid hiding the plane.
object_craft.articulation: Plane orientation is recomputed whenever the grain orientation changes.

object_craft.structure: A line defect with a visible step in the surrounding lattice rows, so the marker has structural evidence around it.
object_craft.material: A single high-contrast accent reserved for the defect; nothing else in the scene may use it.
object_craft.articulation: Advances in discrete steps along the plane and halts at the boundary.

physical_contract.scope: Discrete illustrative stepping of an authored defect; no stress, strain or contact is simulated.
checks: The dislocation marker stops at the boundary of its grain.
Changing a grain orientation rotates lattice, plane and marker together.
